top_signals.title: Building an Arsenal That Survives the Tenth Salvo
top_signals.summary:
America faces a well-defined industrial base problem. Whether it’s a hypothetical Taiwan invasion wargame run two dozen times, the current Iranian conflict, or the Russo-Ukrainian War, the same result repeats: Magazines of key weapons such as cruise missile systems and interceptors empty within days, weeks, or months, and the current industrial base takes years to replenish them. Part of that shortfall results from the analog way in which missile structures are designed, tooled, and sourced, which locks the entire supply chain into rigid, design-specific schedules.The first salvo depends on platforms, positioning, and doctrine, all things controllable by militaries. top_signals.title: Taiwan Commits Up to $4.4 Billion to Alaska LNG Megaproject
top_signals.summary: Taiwan has agreed to invest up to $4.4 billion in the Alaska LNG project and commit to buying 30% of its output over a period of 20 years, President Trump said, as quoted by AFP, during a campaign rally in Alaska. Earlier today, Taiwan confirmed its intention to spend over $4 billion on the Alaska LNG project and commit to buying liquefied gas from the new facility, which is yet to be built, along with a pipeline to carry the gas to the export terminal. top_signals.summary: Shri Piyush Goyal, Union Minister of Commerce & Industry, Republic of India; T.H. Gan Kim Yong, Deputy Prime Minister & Minister for Trade & Industry, Republic of Singapore; Yuvraj Narayan, Group CEO, DP World; and T.H.
